easy.def: Every one of a group, one at a time.
examples: Each child has a book.
I gave each dog a bone.
Each day is new.

more.def: Every one of two or more things or people, thought about separately.
examples: Each student gets a turn to speak.
The teacher gave each child a sticker.
Each flower in the garden is a different color.

easy.def: Wanting to do something very much.
examples: I am eager to see my friends.
The dog is eager for a walk.
We were eager to open our gifts.

more.def: Very excited and interested in doing or having something.
examples: The puppies were eager to go outside and play.
The eager students raised their hands before the question ended.
He was eager to show his parents his report card.

related.def: Wanting very much to do something.

easy.def: With great interest.
examples: The kids waited eagerly.
She eagerly opened the gift.
He eagerly raised his hand.

more.def: In a way that shows you are very keen and want something to happen.
examples: The kids waited eagerly for the bell.
She eagerly opened the box.
He eagerly raised his hand to answer.

easy.def: A big bird that hunts.
examples: The eagle flew high.
An eagle has sharp eyes.
We saw an eagle.

more.def: A large, strong bird with sharp eyes and curved claws that hunts other animals.
examples: The eagle soared above the mountain.
Eagles build huge nests high in trees.
A bald eagle is a symbol of our country.

easy.def: The part of your head you hear with.
examples: I have two ears.
A rabbit has long ears.
Cover your ears.

more.def: The part on the side of the head that you hear with.
examples: The rabbit twitched its long ears.
He whispered in her ear.
Cover your ears when the siren sounds.

easy.def: The part of a corn plant with the kernels.
examples: We ate an ear of corn.
An ear of corn is yellow.
Corn grows on an ear.

more.def: The part of a corn plant that holds the rows of kernels.
examples: Dad grilled an ear of corn.
Each ear of corn has hundreds of kernels.
Farmers pick the ears when they are ripe.

easy.def: A thin skin inside your ear that helps you hear.
examples: The eardrum helps you hear.
A loud noise hurt my eardrum.
Sound shakes the eardrum.

more.def: A thin layer of skin inside the ear that shakes when sound reaches it.
examples: Sound waves make the eardrum vibrate.
A very loud noise can hurt the eardrum.
The doctor looked at her eardrum.

easy.def: The soft part at the bottom of your ear.
examples: I touched my earlobe.
The earlobe is soft.
She wore an earring on her earlobe.

more.def: The soft, rounded part at the bottom of the outer ear.
examples: An earring hung from her earlobe.
The earlobe has no bone in it.
He tugged on his earlobe while he thought.

easy.def: Before the usual time.
examples: I woke up early today.
The bus came early.
We got to school early.

more.def: Before the usual, expected or planned time.
examples: We arrived early to get good seats at the show.
The flowers bloomed early because of the warm spring.
She left early so she would not miss the train.

easy.def: Near the start of a time.
examples: I go for a walk in the early morning.
Early spring has little green buds.
It was an early lesson.

more.def: Happening near the beginning of a period of time.
examples: The early settlers built cabins from logs.
In the early evening, the birds sing loudly.
Early spring brings the first green shoots.

easy.def: To get money for work.
examples: She earns money.
I earned five dollars.
He earns a salary.

more.def: To get money by working.
examples: She earns money walking dogs.
I earned five dollars washing cars.
Dad earns his pay at the factory.

easy.def: To get something by doing well.
examples: You earned a prize.
She earned a star.
He earned a badge.

more.def: To get something because of what you have done.
examples: You earned a prize for your hard work.
She earned a gold star on her paper.
He earned a badge for swimming.

easy.def: Serious and sincere.
examples: He is earnest.
An earnest effort.
She gave an earnest answer.

more.def: Serious, honest and sincere about what you are doing.
examples: He made an earnest effort to learn the song.
She gave an earnest answer to the question.
The earnest student worked hard on every lesson.

easy.def: Money you get for work.
examples: His earnings were small.
She saved her earnings.
I spent my earnings.

more.def: The money that a person gets from doing work.
examples: She saved her earnings from the lemonade stand.
His earnings from the summer job were small.
The company's earnings grew this year.

easy.def: A small speaker you wear in your ear.
examples: He wore an earpiece.
The earpiece is small.
She took out the earpiece.

more.def: A small device worn in the ear to hear sound.
examples: The reporter wore an earpiece.
He put the earpiece in his ear to listen.
The phone has an earpiece.

easy.def: A small plug you put in your ear to block sound.
examples: I wear earplugs.
An earplug is soft.
She put in an earplug.

more.def: A small plug that is put in the ear to keep out noise or water.
examples: I wore earplugs at the loud concert.
She put an earplug in each ear.
Swimmers wear earplugs to keep water out.

easy.def: A piece of jewelry for the ear.
examples: She wears earrings.
The earring is gold.
I lost an earring.

more.def: A small piece of jewelry that is worn on the ear.
examples: She wore silver earrings to the party.
I lost an earring at the park.
The earring sparkled in the light.

easy.def: The planet we live on.
examples: The Earth goes around the sun.
Earth is our home.
Astronauts see the Earth from space.

more.def: The planet we live on, the third planet from the sun.
examples: Earth takes a year to travel around the sun.
From space, Earth looks blue and white.
Earth is the only planet we know that has life.

easy.def: The ground that plants grow in.
examples: The earth is wet.
He dug into the earth.
Plants grow in the earth.

more.def: The soil or ground that plants grow in.
examples: The farmer pressed the seeds into the earth.
After the rain, the earth smelled fresh.
Worms tunnel through the earth.

related.def: To dig something up out of the ground.

easy.def: Having to do with the Earth or this life.
examples: Earthly life.
An earthly paradise.
Earthly things.

more.def: Having to do with the Earth and ordinary life, rather than heaven or the spirit.
examples: The monk gave up earthly pleasures.
The old tale describes an earthly paradise.
There is no earthly reason to be afraid.

easy.def: When the ground shakes.
examples: The earthquake made the house shake.
We hid under the desk in the earthquake.
An earthquake can crack a road.

more.def: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement deep inside the Earth.
examples: The earthquake knocked books off the shelves.
The bridge was built to stay standing in an earthquake.
Scientists measure how strong each earthquake is.

easy.def: A long, thin, soft animal that lives in the soil.
examples: An earthworm crawled on the path.
The earthworm is pink.
We found an earthworm.

more.def: A long, soft, thin animal that lives in soil and helps keep it healthy.
examples: An earthworm crawled across the wet path after the rain.
Earthworms eat dead plants and help the soil.
We found an earthworm when we dug in the garden.

easy.def: Doing something without trouble.
examples: She won with ease.
He lifted it with ease.
The cat climbed with ease.

more.def: The lack of trouble when doing something, so that it seems easy.
examples: She climbed the tree with ease.
He did the puzzle with ease.
The ease of the game made it fun for little kids.

easy.def: To make pain or work feel lighter.
examples: The medicine will ease the pain.
A cool cloth eased the burn.
The rain eased.

more.def: To make something less painful, hard or strong.
examples: A cold cloth will ease the pain.
The rain eased in the afternoon.
He eased the door open so it would not squeak.

easy.def: Without trouble.
examples: I can easily lift it.
She easily won the race.
The cat easily jumped the fence.

more.def: In a way that is easy and does not need much effort.
examples: She easily solved the puzzle.
The cat jumped the fence easily.
He can easily carry that bag.

easy.def: The direction where the sun comes up.
examples: The sun rises in the east.
We drove east.
Birds flew east.

more.def: The direction opposite to west, where the sun rises.
examples: Morning light spills in from the east.
Our house faces east.
They traveled east across the country.

easy.def: Going toward the east.
examples: The eastbound train left.
An eastbound bus.
The eastbound road is closed.

more.def: Traveling or leading toward the east.
examples: The eastbound train left the station.
Traffic on the eastbound road was slow.
We took the eastbound bus.

easy.def: Having to do with the east.
examples: The eastern sky is bright.
The eastern part of the state.
He lives in the eastern town.

more.def: Found in, coming from or toward the east.
examples: The sun rises in the eastern sky.
The eastern coast has many beaches.
We drove to the eastern side of the lake.

easy.def: Not hard to do.
examples: The test was easy.
This game is easy.
It is easy to read.

more.def: Not difficult, and needing little effort.
examples: The puzzle was easy, so we finished it in five minutes.
Riding a bike is easy once you learn how.
It is easy to find the school because it is so big.

easy.def: To put food in your mouth and swallow it.
examples: I eat lunch.
The cow eats grass.
We ate pizza.

more.def: To take food into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.
examples: Rabbits eat grass, carrots, and lettuce.
We ate sandwiches by the river.
Have you eaten breakfast yet?

easy.def: A person or animal that eats.
examples: She is a fast eater.
The baby is a messy eater.
The cat is a picky eater.

more.def: A person or an animal that eats, especially in a certain way or a certain kind of food.
examples: My little brother is a slow eater and takes an hour to finish dinner.
The panda is a bamboo eater and eats for twelve hours a day.
She is a picky eater and will only eat plain pasta.

easy.def: To listen secretly to people talking.
examples: Do not eavesdrop.
She eavesdropped at the door.
He tried to eavesdrop.

more.def: To listen secretly to a private talk.
examples: It is rude to eavesdrop on other people.
She eavesdropped at the door and heard the surprise.
He tried to eavesdrop on the grown-ups.
